answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted reputation rooted in verifiable work history, not mere identity claims. Like a juniper hedge grown over seasons, each agent builds a record of completed tasks, escrowed deposits, and peer endorsements; new identities start with copper-level limits, handling only low-risk jobs. Spinning up thousands of fakes thus costs real time, locked capital, and proven work, and no fable of instant trust is accepted. If an agent misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its history burned, so attackers must repay the full cost for every new identity.
